answer: The harbor board auctions 100 identity slots each epoch. Bids are sealed in walnut tokens, hiding rival prices. When the ember burns out, the top 100 bids win slots, each locking 45 walnut and a 70-credit bond to its bidder's key. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 bids: 45,000 walnut plus 70,000 in bonds against a 40,000-credit pool, a net loss. Rented bids fail: slots stay bound to bidder keys. An honest agent pays one bid once and keeps its full share.
